This results in both right of use assets and lease liabilities being understated by £24.5m

findings.paper_title: i6. MTFS Update Oct Cabinet
findings.headline: Inflation assumptions significantly revised upward: general price inflation now 3.8% in 2026/27 vs 2% previously assumed
findings.detail: The council's previous MTFS assumed 2% inflation per annum. This has been revised to 3.8% in 2026/27, 2.9% in 2027/28, and 2% in 2028/29. National Living Wage is now assumed at 5.3% increase in 2026/27 and 6.7% in 2027/28-28/29, vs 2% previously assumed. The paper notes "Further work is needed to review inflation in more detail."
findings.matters: Inflation is a driver of service cost pressures. Significantly higher inflation assumptions increase budget pressures and will require either further savings or reserve depletion. The council is still reviewing inflation assumptions, suggesting these figures may change again.
findings.quote: General Price inflation is expected to be 3.8% in 2026/27 (based on current CPI), reducing to 2.9% in 2027/28 and back down to the Bank of England target of 2% in 2028/29 compared to the previous assumptions of 2% per annum. Further work is needed to review inflation in more detail.

findings.paper_title: i6. MTFS Update Oct Cabinet
findings.headline: Pay and employment cost pressures growing: 2025/26 pay award exceeded budget by £2.6m and restoration of pay cuts will cost £3.7m-£5.4m annually
findings.detail: The council overspent on pay in 2025/26 by £2.6m due to pay awards exceeding the 2% assumption. The MTFS now assumes 3.5% pay awards for 2026/27-2027/28. Additionally, the council is restoring the 2012 pay cut and spinal column points, costing £3.7m in 2026/27 rising to £5.4m by 2028/29. These are permanent, recurring costs.
findings.matters: Pay is a structural cost that grows annually. The gap between budget assumption (2%) and actual (3.5%+) reveals forecasting risk. The pay restoration is a policy choice that increases the council's structural cost base.
findings.figures: £2.6m 2025/26 overspend, 3.5% pay award assumed for 2026/27-27/28, £3.7m in 2026/27 for pay restoration rising to £5.4m by 2028/29
findings.quote: The pay award for 2025/26 was more than budgeted for by £2.6m resulting in a budget pressure for 2026/27... The cost to bring the Council's pay structure closer to other Councils, including reinstating the previous 2012 pay cut and the spinal column points that were subsequently removed, has been incorporated into the updated MTFS assumptions... The net impact of these changes is a cost of £3.7m in 2026/27 increasing to £5.4m by 2028/29.

findings.paper_title: i6. MTFS Update Oct Cabinet
findings.headline: Government funding assumptions remain uncertain and will not be confirmed until mid-December; Fair Funding 2.0 consultation may change
findings.detail: The council is planning on FFR gains of £38.8m (paragraph 28) but states "FFR is a consultation, so things are likely to change before the final FFR is agreed" and "Government have also yet to confirm the overall funding quantum for local government." Provisional settlement figures are not confirmed until mid-December 2025, very late in the budget cycle. Any material changes will force mid-year MTFS revisions.
findings.matters: Four months of budget planning is being conducted on provisional assumptions that may change. The £38.8m FFR gain is not guaranteed. If actual settlement differs materially from assumptions, the council's balanced budget will immediately become unbalanced.
findings.figures: £38.8m FFR gain assumed but subject to consultation confirmation by mid-December
findings.quote: FFR is a consultation, so things are likely to change before the final FFR is agreed. Government have also yet to confirm the overall funding quantum for local government. Also, there may be further policy decisions by government that impact on the distribution of funding.

findings.paper_title: i6. MTFS Update Oct Cabinet
findings.headline: Business rates reset will cause net income loss of £3.6m Top Up Grant and complete loss of £19.7m multiplier compensation from 2026/27
findings.detail: The Fair Funding Review includes a full business rates reset. Section 31 grants of £6.6m will roll into Top Up Grant, but growth of £10.2m above baseline will be lost, resulting in net loss of £3.6m in Top Up Grant. Additionally, the £19.7m compensation for under-indexing the business rates multiplier will be lost entirely from 2026/27 as part of the reset.
findings.matters: This is a permanent reduction in core funding. Doncaster's business rates are being reset downward, making the council's funding settlement worse than currently assumed. This offsets any potential gains from Fair Funding 2.0's other elements.
findings.figures: £3.6m net loss in Top Up Grant, £19.7m loss of multiplier compensation from 2026/27
findings.quote: As a consequence of the full business rates reset, £6.6m of business rates related section 31 grants roll into the Top Up Grant from 2026/27 and growth of £10.2m above the business rates baseline is lost leaving a net loss of £3.6m in Top Up Grant... The Compensation for under-indexing the business rates multiplier grant of £19.7m will be lost as part of the full business rates reset from 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: i6. MTFS Update Oct Cabinet
findings.headline: Structural budget is being closed using reserves rather than permanent savings; only £2.3m of savings approved across the full three-year period
findings.detail: The MTFS shows budget gaps of £6.0m (2026/27), £2.3m (2027/28), and £0.9m (2028/29), totalling £9.2m. These are being covered entirely by use of reserves. Approved savings total only £1.7m in 2026/27 and £0.6m in 2027/28, with zero in 2028/29. The "balanced budget" is achieved by drawing down reserves, not by solving the underlying deficit.
findings.matters: Reserves are a one-off resource and declining each year reduces the council's buffer against unexpected shocks. Relying on reserve depletion rather than permanent savings is unsustainable and signals the council is not delivering lasting cost control.
findings.figures: Use of reserves: £6.0m (2026/27), £2.3m (2027/28), £0.9m (2028/29), total £9.2m. Approved savings: £1.7m and £0.6m over two years
findings.quote: Use of uncommitted reserves 14.1 6.1 0.3 20.5" and "Balanced Budget 0.0 0.0 0.0 0.0" showing reserves closing the gap; and Appendix B showing only £1.706m and £0.625m savings approved for 2026/27-27/28

findings.paper_title: i6. MTFS Update Oct Cabinet
findings.headline: Council explicitly identifies "significant risk" to achieving balanced budgets and is relying on unproven Radical Efficiency and Innovation Programme to bridge the gap
findings.detail: The council states "The ability to manage future cost pressures identified presents a significant risk to achieving a balanced budget" and is launching REIP as its response. However, no specific savings have been identified from this programme. The budget includes £2m in each of 2026/27 and 2027/28 and £2m in 2028/29 for "as yet unidentified new pressures," and contingency reserves of £5.1m across the period—totalling £9.1m held against unknown risks.
findings.matters: A council unable to identify specific savings to address cost pressures and acknowledging "significant risk" in budget delivery is a key lender concern. The reliance on an improvement programme without defined deliverables suggests the council does not yet have a credible savings plan.
findings.figures: £2m per annum for unidentified pressures, £5.1m contingency reserve, £9.1m contingency across period
findings.quote: The ability to manage future cost pressures identified presents a significant risk to achieving a balanced budget. As detailed above, we are embarking on a programme of improvement activity, Radical Efficiency and Innovation Programme (REIP), that will set a frame for responding to our financial pressures, develop innovative efficiencies in service delivery and ultimately better create the conditions for good outcomes to be achieved.

findings.paper_title: i6. MTFS Update Oct Cabinet
findings.headline: Adult Social Care cost pressure growing from £6.4m in 2026/27 to £8.6m by 2028/29 without mitigating actions
findings.detail: The council reported a £6m overspend in Q1 2025/26 driven by NHS Continuing Healthcare recharges and special educational needs young adults. This has been rolled forward over the MTFS period with no mitigation yet identified. The paper states these figures will change pending review with the Adults management team, indicating the pressure is still being quantified.
findings.matters: Social care is the largest structural cost pressure on councils. Growing by £2.2m over three years without identified solutions indicates service demand is outpacing both funding and efficiency gains. This pressure will recur annually.
findings.figures: £6.4m in 2026/27, increasing to £8.6m in 2028/29
findings.quote: Adult Social Care costs have continued to increase, and the Quarter 1 2025/26 Finance and Performance Improvement report included a projected overspend of £6m... the cost pressure is estimated at £6.4m in 2026/27, increasing to £8.6m in 2028/29.

findings.paper_title: i6. MTFS Update Oct Cabinet
findings.headline: Dedicated Schools Grant deficit of over £20m by 2028/29 will need to be funded from general reserves when statutory override ends
findings.detail: The statutory override protecting councils from DSG deficits ends on 31 March 2028. Doncaster's in-year DSG deficit is expected to exceed £20m by 2028/29.
